newsitem.title: UK: Oxford Biomedica slumps below issue price.
newsitem.headline: Oxford Biomedica slumps below issue price.

text.p: Shares in Britain's Oxford Biomedica slumped at their debut on the Alternative Investment Market (AIM), quoted at 50-1/2 pence, or 42.6 percent below the issue price of 88 pence.
The fact two underwiters were trying to pull out was weighing on the shares, said Oxford Biomedica's chief executive Alan Kingsman.

"We had some technical problems with underwriters and the market is probably reacting to that," Kingsman told Reuters. "We are currently looking at our legal position versus two underwriters who have not fullfilled their obligations."
The two underwriters who tried to pull out were Stockton Trading - a Bahamaian registered company - and private investor Kaj Kjellquist from Sweden, said sponsoring broker Teather & Greenwood.

Commenting on the first day of trading, Percy Lomax, corporate financier at Teather & Greenwood said: "It is a disappointment. Obviously people were nervous...and what we are trying to do is to build the price up."
